   131	## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
   132	- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
   133	- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
   134	- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
   135	
   136	## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
   137	Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
   138	from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
   139	look as if the paper stated them.
   140	
   141	- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
   142	  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
   143	- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
   144	  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
   145	  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
   146	  anchored paper passage, or blueprint label it supports. Blueprint line
   147	  ranges are derived review context, not stored docstring citations; resolve a
   148	  label with `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve <label>`.
   149	- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
   150	  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
   151	  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
   152	  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
   153	  Lean proof.
   154	- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
   155	  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
   156	  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
   157	  used.
   158	- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
   159	  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
   160	  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
   161	  proof remains tracked as incomplete.
   162	
   163	## Blueprint Structure
   164	- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.
   165	- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`
   166	- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`
   167	
   168	## Lean Blueprint Macros
   169	- `\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration
   170	- `\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see "Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`" below
   171	- `\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph
   172	- `\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)
   173	- `\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)
   174	
   175	### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`
   176	
   177	`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.
   178	
   179	**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.
   180	
   181	**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).
   182	
   183	A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.
   184	
   185	Excerpt from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`:
   186	
   187	```latex
   188	\begin{theorem}[Commutativity of the point measurements]\label{thm:commutativity-points}
   189	  \lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.CommutativityPoints.commutativityPoints}
   190	  \leanok
   191	  \uses{def:good-strategy, def:approx_delta}
   192	  Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy.
   193	\end{theorem}
   194	\begin{proof}
   195	  \leanok
   196	  The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$.
   197	\end{proof}
   198	```
   199	
   200	**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.
   201	
   202	`leanblueprint` does not use distinct macro names for these two claims, so audits must distinguish them by environment context rather than by raw `\leanok` counts. A future split such as `\leanokstmt` / `\leanokproof` could make that distinction explicit, but that is only a possible later cleanup; the current convention is to keep `\leanok` and rely on placement.
   203	
   204	A recurring historical example is the chapter 4 `Q/X/\widehat X/P` witness
   205	layer.  Once Lean has construction theorems deriving the displayed identities
   206	and estimates from the rank-reduction, sigma-range, positive-Gram, native

   214	- **Light green box**: definition with `\lean` + `\leanok` (defined in Lean)

   220	## Bibliography Workflow
   221	1. Edit `blueprint/src/references.bib` (standalone, AuthorYYYYKeyword keys)
   222	2. Run `texra-blueprint bbl` from the repository root — it regenerates
   223	   `blueprint/src/web.bbl` from the `\cite` keys in the blueprint sources.
   224	   `web.bbl` is not committed (`.gitignore` covers `*.bbl`); every CI job
   225	   that runs the web build regenerates it first, and so must a local run.
   226	3. Run `leanblueprint web` (plasTeX reads `web.bbl`)
   227	4. The PDF build needs no separate step: `leanblueprint pdf` runs bibtex on
   228	   `print.tex` itself, and `print.bbl` never feeds the web build.
   229	5. Citation key format: e.g., `Ji2020MIPStar`, `Natarajan2020Quantum`
   230	6. Paper-gap notes: blueprint prose cites `\cite{gap:<slug>}` (never the raw
   231	   `docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex` path); each cited note has a `@techreport`
   232	   entry in `blueprint/src/references.bib` with `type = {Paper-gap note}`,
   233	   whose `note` field carries the published PDF URL as `\url{...}` (the
   234	   alpha style of the PDF build drops `url` fields for techreport entries).
   235	   `texra-blueprint bbl` renders such entries with slug-shaped citation
   236	   labels (e.g. `[issue-906-main-formal-k-bound]`) in the web bibliography,
   237	   while ordinary entries keep alpha labels. Lean docstrings and comments
   238	   keep the repository path form.

   240	## Stale/Corrupt Aux File Recovery
   241	If LaTeX reports `! File ended while scanning use of \@newl@bel` on startup:
   242	- The `.aux` file was truncated by a previous killed/timed-out run
   243	- Fix: `rm -f blueprint/src/print.aux blueprint/print/print.aux blueprint/print.aux`
   244	- Then rerun latexmk — it rebuilds the aux from scratch cleanly
   245	- `web.bbl` is unaffected: it comes from `texra-blueprint bbl`, not from
   246	  `print.bbl`

   251	leanblueprint web     # HTML → blueprint/web/

   253	leanblueprint all     # pdf + web + checkdecls

    98	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, formalizing the
    99	unlabelled observation at
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1049-1051`.
   101	`Distribution.bind` is the finite uniform-mixture operation.  The two halves
   102	are proved from the equal-fiber decomposition of `chiIndex` and the fact that
   103	every line conditioning map retains the shared scalar seed. -/
   104	theorem linePointDist_eq_mixture_restricted (L : LdParams) :
   105	    aLinePointDist L =
   106	        Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m))
   107	          (restrictedALineDist L) ∧
   108	      dLinePointDist L =
   109	        Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m))
   110	          (restrictedDLineDist L) :=
   111	  ⟨aLinePointDist_eq_bind_restricted L, dLinePointDist_eq_bind_restricted L⟩
   112	
   113	/-- Restricting a nonnegative average from the line-point distribution to one
   114	fixed line kind and coordinate inflates its bound by at most `2m`.
   115	
   116	**Source statement:** item 1 of blueprint
   117	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, from the unlabelled
   118	estimate at
   119	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1056`.
   120	The restricted component carries mixture weight `1 / (2m)`, so a nonnegative
   121	average bounded by `δ` bounds it by `2mδ`. -/
   122	theorem avg_restricted_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   123	    (f : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) -> ℝ)
   124	    (hf : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ f sample) {δ : ℝ}
   125	    (havg : avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f ≤ δ)
   126	    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
   127	    avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i) f ≤
   128	      2 * (P.m : ℝ) * δ := by
   129	  refine (avgOver_restrictedLinePointDist_le f hf kind i).trans ?_
   130	  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left havg (by positivity)
   131	
   132	/-- Restricting both variables of a nonnegative average over two independent
   133	line-point samples inflates its bound by at most `4m^2`.
   134	
   135	**Source statement:** item 2 of blueprint
   136	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, from the unlabelled
   137	estimate at
   138	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1056-1058`.
   139	The one-variable estimate is applied successively to the two product

   141	theorem avg_restricted_prod_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   142	    (f : ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) ×
   143	      (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))) -> ℝ)
   144	    (hf : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ f sample) {δ : ℝ}
   145	    (havg : avgOver
   146	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
   147	        (linePointDist P.toLdParams)) f ≤ δ)
   148	    (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :
   149	    avgOver
   150	      (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
   151	        (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j)) f ≤
   152	      4 * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * δ := by
   153	  refine (avgOver_prod_restrictedLinePointDist_le f hf kindX kindZ i j).trans ?_
   154	  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left havg (by positivity)
   155	
   156	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary for item 3 of
   157	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`: a consistency defect of two complete
   158	measurements placed on opposite registers inflates by at most `4m^2` when
   159	both line-point coordinates are restricted.  Blueprint
   160	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
   161	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1058-1061`. -/
   162	private theorem consistencyDefect_restricted_prod_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   163	    {ε δ : ℝ} {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   164	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
   165	    (M₁ : ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) ×
   166	        (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))) ->
   167	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
   168	    (M₂ : ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) ×
   169	        (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))) ->
   170	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side))
   171	    (hbound : consistencyDefect
   172	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
   173	        (linePointDist P.toLdParams))
   174	      (fun sample answer => S.place p₁ ((M₁ sample).effect answer))
   175	      (fun sample answer => S.place p₂ ((M₂ sample).effect answer))
   176	      S.psiHat ≤ δ)
   177	    (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :
   178	    consistencyDefect
   179	      (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
   180	        (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j))
   181	      (fun sample answer => S.place p₁ ((M₁ sample).effect answer))
   182	      (fun sample answer => S.place p₂ ((M₂ sample).effect answer))
   183	      S.psiHat ≤ 4 * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * δ := by
   184	  unfold consistencyDefect at hbound ⊢
   185	  refine le_trans
   186	    (avgOver_prod_restrictedLinePointDist_le _ ?_ kindX kindZ i j) ?_
   187	  · intro sample
   188	    exact consistencyDefect_integrand_nonneg S p₁ p₂ hopp (M₁ sample)
   189	      (M₂ sample)
   190	  · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbound (by positivity)
   191	
   192	/-- The evaluated joint line measurement remains consistent with the joint
   193	point measurement on every product of restricted line distributions.
   194	
   195	**Source statement:** item 3 and Equation `eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted` of
   196	blueprint
   197	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, from
   198	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1058-1061`.
   199	Here `consistencyDefect` is the finite POVM form of the displayed expectation
   200	against `Id - Q` after both measurements are postprocessed by evaluation.
   201	The universal constant is outside all strategy and parameter quantifiers, and
   202	is the exact inflation factor `4` of `avg_restricted_prod_le`. -/
   203	theorem restricted_lines_consistency_bound :
   204	    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
   205	      ∀ {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
   206	        (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	        (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   208	        (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
   209	        (p1 p2 : Placement), p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   210	        ∀ (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m),
   211	          consistencyDefect
   212	            (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
   213	              (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j))
   214	            (fun sample answer => S.place p1
   215	              (((lines.T p1.side sample.1.1 sample.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   216	                (evalOpt sample.1.1 sample.1.2 fs.1,
   217	                  evalOpt sample.2.1 sample.2.2 fs.2)).effect answer))
   218	            (fun sample answer => S.place p2
   219	              (((points.Q p2.side sample.1.2 sample.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   220	                (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect answer))
   221	            S.psiHat ≤ C * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * δP := by
   222	  refine ⟨4, by norm_num, ?_⟩
   223	  intro P ε δQ δP S points lines p1 p2 hopp kindX kindZ i j
   224	  exact consistencyDefect_restricted_prod_le S p1 p2 hopp
   225	    (fun sample => (lines.T p1.side sample.1.1 sample.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   226	      (evalOpt sample.1.1 sample.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt sample.2.1 sample.2.2 fs.2))
   227	    (fun sample => (points.Q p2.side sample.1.2 sample.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   228	      (some ab.1, some ab.2))
   229	    (lines.consistent p1 p2 hopp) kindX kindZ i j
   230	
   231	/-! ## The sub-line distribution -/
   232	
   233	/-- Existence of the directly indexed sub-line distribution with its two
   234	separate projected point marginals and axis-line closure.  It supports
   235	`lem:qld-sublines` and `rem:qld-sublines-property-three` in
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, whose source is
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1069` with
   238	its proof at lines 1071--1116.
   239	
   240	This is a formalization auxiliary assertion, not the source-labelled
   241	`lem:qld-sublines`.  The extended line uses the directly indexed carrier and
   242	line-point law of `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` in
   243	place of the seed-indexed line-point distribution over `F_q^(2m+2)` of the
   244	source statement, so the statement carries no divisibility hypothesis and its
   245	transport to the source carrier remains open.  Its `source_mixture` field
   246	asserts only the separate X and Z marginal mixtures, not a stronger joint
   247	conditional law.
   248	
   249	The witness is the sub-line law `subLineDist` of the sampling procedure.  Its
   250	pointwise fields follow from `subLineTripleOf_incidence`,
   251	`subLineTripleOf_compatibility`, and `subLineTripleOf_axis_closure`, after

   253	Its extended-line marginal is `subLineDist_map_fst`, and its two projected
   254	point marginals are the separate mixtures of `subLineDist_source_mixture`. -/
   255	theorem exists_subLineWitness (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   256	    Nonempty (SubLineWitness P) := by
   257	  refine ⟨{ D := subLineDist P
   258	            isProbability := subLineDist_isProbability P
   259	            extended_marginal := subLineDist_map_fst P
   260	            incidence := ?_
   261	            compatibility := ?_
   262	            source_mixture := subLineDist_source_mixture P
   263	            axis_closure := ?_ }⟩
   264	  · intro sample hsample u hu
   265	    obtain ⟨kind, k, w, hx, hz, rfl⟩ :=
   266	      exists_raw_of_mem_subLineDist_support P hsample
   267	    exact subLineTripleOf_incidence P kind k w hx hz hu
   268	  · intro sample hsample
   269	    obtain ⟨kind, k, w, hx, hz, rfl⟩ :=
   270	      exists_raw_of_mem_subLineDist_support P hsample
   271	    exact subLineTripleOf_compatibility P kind k w hx hz
   272	  · intro sample hsample haxis
   273	    obtain ⟨kind, k, w, hx, hz, rfl⟩ :=
   274	      exists_raw_of_mem_subLineDist_support P hsample

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Witnesses
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.Calculus
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# The ordered point product on a single placement
     6	
     7	The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
     8	with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
     9	The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
    10	families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
    11	joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
    12	triangle inequality twice.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
    18	`Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    27	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
    32	between the two members of each pair. -/
    33	theorem Placement.exists_isOpposite (p : Placement) :
    34	    ∃ q : Placement, p.IsOpposite q ∧ q.IsOpposite p := by
    35	  cases p with
    36	  | AA' => exact ⟨.BA'', trivial, trivial⟩
    37	  | BA'' => exact ⟨.AA', trivial, trivial⟩
    38	  | BB' => exact ⟨.AB'', trivial, trivial⟩
    39	  | AB'' => exact ⟨.BB', trivial, trivial⟩
    40	
    41	/-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
    42	`Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
    43	theorem CombinedPointsWitness.orderedZX_dist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    44	    {ε δ : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
    45	    (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) (p : Placement) :
    46	    opFamilyDistSq
    47	        (uniformDistribution
    48	          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    49	        (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    50	        (fun xz ab => S.place p
    51	          ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    52	            (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    53	        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * δ := by
    54	  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hqp⟩ := p.exists_isOpposite
    55	  have htri := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le
    56	    (uniformDistribution
    57	      ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    58	    (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    59	    (fun xz ab => S.place q ((points.Q q.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    60	    (fun xz ab => S.place p
    61	      ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    62	        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    63	    S.psiHat δ δ (points.self_consistent p q hpq)
    64	    (points.consistent_ZX q p hqp)
    65	  linarith
    66	
    67	end
    68	
    69	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.Support
     2	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.SwitchSandwichPrep.InnerProduct
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Replacing one factor of a measurement-weighted overlap
     6	
     7	The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases compare averaged
     8	overlaps whose left factor is one complete measurement and whose right factors
     9	are operator families at small state-dependent distance.  This module records
    10	the corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.  The right-hand families are
    11	arbitrary, so the estimate covers an ordered product of point effects, which
    12	is not itself a measurement.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The estimate is `lem:overlap-gap-distance` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it is the Cauchy--Schwarz
    18	step at paper
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1147-1166`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    27	open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus
    28	
    29	/-- Replacing one operator family inside an overlap weighted on the left by a
    30	complete measurement changes the average by at most the square root of the
    31	state-dependent squared distance between the two families. -/
    32	theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    33	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    34	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B C : X → α → Op ι)
    35	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    36	    (ζ : ℝ) (hBC : opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ ≤ ζ) :
    37	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) -
    38	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))| ≤
    39	      Real.sqrt ζ := by
    40	  classical
    41	  have hnorm_sq : ∀ M : Op ι,
    42	      ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ ^ 2 = stateQForm ψ (Mᴴ * M) := by
    43	    intro M
    44	    rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
    45	    unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
    46	    rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
    47	    change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ)).re =
    48	      (inner ℂ ψ ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint
    49	        (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ))).re
    50	    rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
    51	  have hmul : ∀ M N : Op ι, Mᴴ = M →
    52	      stateQForm ψ (M * N) =
    53	        (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState M ψ)
    54	          (applyOperatorToState N ψ)).re := by
    55	    intro M N hM
    56	    have hadjoint : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint =
    57	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin M := by
    58	      rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, hM]
    59	    calc
    60	      stateQForm ψ (M * N) =
    61	          (inner ℂ ψ
    62	            (applyOperatorToState M (applyOperatorToState N ψ))).re := by
    63	        rw [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState_mul]
    64	      _ = (inner ℂ ψ ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint
    65	            (applyOperatorToState N ψ))).re := by
    66	        rw [hadjoint]
    67	        rfl
    68	      _ = _ := by
    69	        rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
    70	        rfl
    71	  have hleft : ∀ x : X,
    72	      (∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 := by
    73	    intro x
    74	    have htotal : (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a)) = 1 := by
    75	      calc
    76	        (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a)) =
    77	            stateQForm ψ (∑ a : α, (A x).effect a) := by
    78	          simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
    79	        _ = stateQForm ψ 1 := by rw [(A x).sum_eq_one]
    80	        _ = 1 := by rw [stateQForm]; simp [applyOperatorToState, hψ]
    81	    calc
    82	      (∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤
    83	          ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a) := by
    84	        refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
    85	        intro a _
    86	        rw [hnorm_sq, measurement_effect_hermitian]
    87	        exact quadratic_form_mono (MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self ((A x).pos a)
    88	          (measurement_effect_le_one (A x) a)) ψ
    89	      _ = 1 := htotal
    90	  have hgnonneg : ∀ x : X,
    91	      0 ≤ ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (B x a - C x a) ψ‖ ^ 2 :=
    92	    fun x => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => sq_nonneg _
    93	  have hpoint : ∀ x : X,
    94	      |∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a - C x a))| ≤
    95	        Real.sqrt (∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (B x a - C x a) ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
    96	    intro x
    97	    let u : α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι := fun a =>
    98	      applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a) ψ
    99	    let v : α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι := fun a =>
   100	      applyOperatorToState (B x a - C x a) ψ
   101	    have hrw : (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a - C x a))) =
   102	        ∑ a : α, (inner ℂ (u a) (v a)).re := by
   103	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   104	      intro a _
   105	      exact hmul _ _ (measurement_effect_hermitian (A x) a)
   106	    have hone : Real.sqrt (∑ a : α, ‖u a‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 := by
   107	      rw [← Real.sqrt_one]
   108	      exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (hleft x)
   109	    calc
   110	      |∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a - C x a))| =
   111	          |∑ a : α, (inner ℂ (u a) (v a)).re| := by rw [hrw]
   112	      _ ≤ ∑ a : α, |(inner ℂ (u a) (v a)).re| :=
   113	        Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   114	      _ ≤ ∑ a : α, ‖u a‖ * ‖v a‖ := by
   115	        refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
   116	        intro a _
   117	        exact (Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans (norm_inner_le_norm (u a) (v a))
   118	      _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ a : α, ‖u a‖ ^ 2) * Real.sqrt (∑ a : α, ‖v a‖ ^ 2) := by
   119	        simpa using Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt
   120	          (Finset.univ : Finset α) (fun a => ‖u a‖) (fun a => ‖v a‖)
   121	      _ ≤ 1 * Real.sqrt (∑ a : α, ‖v a‖ ^ 2) :=
   122	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hone (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
   123	      _ = Real.sqrt (∑ a : α,
   124	            ‖applyOperatorToState (B x a - C x a) ψ‖ ^ 2) := one_mul _
   125	  have hdiff :
   126	      avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) -
   127	          avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α,
   128	            stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) =
   129	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α,
   130	          stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a - C x a))) := by
   131	    rw [← avgOver_sub]
   132	    refine avgOver_congr μ _ _ ?_
   133	    intro x
   134	    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   135	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   136	    intro a _
   137	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   138	  rw [hdiff]
   139	  refine le_trans
   140	    (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.avgOver_abs_le_sqrt_of_pointwise μ _ _
   141	      hpoint hgnonneg (by rw [hμ.weight_sum_eq_one])) ?_
   142	  exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hBC
   143	
   144	/-! ## The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality weighted by a positive operator -/
   145	
   146	/-- For a positive operator `A`, the sesquilinear form `⟨u, A v⟩` satisfies the
   147	Cauchy--Schwarz inequality with the two diagonal values `⟨u, A u⟩` and
   148	`⟨v, A v⟩`.  This is the inequality behind the Cauchy--Schwarz steps of the
   149	proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, in which both factors carry
   150	the square root of the line effect, paper
   151	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
   152	theorem norm_inner_applyOperatorToState_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {ι : Type*}
   153	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : Op ι} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
   154	    (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   155	    ‖inner ℂ u (applyOperatorToState A v)‖ ≤
   156	      Real.sqrt (inner ℂ u (applyOperatorToState A u)).re *
   157	        Real.sqrt (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState A v)).re := by
   158	  set R : Op ι := CFC.sqrt A with hR
   159	  have hRnonneg : 0 ≤ R := CFC.sqrt_nonneg A
   160	  have hRR : R * R = A := CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self A hA
   161	  have hRherm : Rᴴ = R :=
   162	    (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hRnonneg).isHermitian.eq
   163	  have hadjoint : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R).adjoint = Matrix.toEuclideanLin R := by
   164	    rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, hRherm]
   165	  have hsplit : ∀ w z : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
   166	      inner ℂ w (applyOperatorToState A z) =
   167	        inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState R w) (applyOperatorToState R z) := by
   168	    intro w z
   169	    have h := LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R) w
   170	      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R z)
   171	    rw [hadjoint] at h
   172	    rw [← hRR, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   173	    exact h
   174	  have hnorm : ∀ w : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
   175	      ‖applyOperatorToState R w‖ =
   176	        Real.sqrt (inner ℂ w (applyOperatorToState A w)).re := by
   177	    intro w
   178	    have h2 : ‖applyOperatorToState R w‖ ^ 2 =
   179	        (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState R w) (applyOperatorToState R w)).re := by
   180	      rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
   181	      rfl
   182	    rw [hsplit, ← h2, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
   183	  rw [hsplit, ← hnorm, ← hnorm]
   184	  exact norm_inner_le_norm _ _
   185	
   186	/-- The sum over outcomes of the real parts of `⟨u a, A a (v a)⟩`, for
   187	positive weights `A a`, is bounded by the product of the square roots of the
   188	two diagonal sums. -/
   189	theorem abs_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   190	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : α → Op ι) (hA : ∀ a, 0 ≤ A a)
   191	    (u v : α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   192	    |∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re| ≤
   193	      Real.sqrt (∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re) *
   194	        Real.sqrt (∑ a, (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re) := by
   195	  have hu : ∀ a, 0 ≤ (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re :=
   196	    fun a => stateQForm_nonneg (u a) (hA a)
   197	  have hv : ∀ a, 0 ≤ (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re :=
   198	    fun a => stateQForm_nonneg (v a) (hA a)
   199	  calc
   200	    |∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re|
   201	        ≤ ∑ a, |(inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re| :=
   202	      Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   203	    _ ≤ ∑ a, Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re *
   204	          Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re := by
   205	      refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
   206	      exact (Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans
   207	        (norm_inner_applyOperatorToState_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt (hA a) (u a) (v a))
   208	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ a,
   209	            Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re ^ 2) *
   210	          Real.sqrt (∑ a,
   211	            Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re ^ 2) :=
   212	      Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt _ _ _
   213	    _ = _ := by
   214	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Real.sq_sqrt (hu a),
   215	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Real.sq_sqrt (hv a)]
   216	
   217	/-- The averaged form of the preceding estimate: the average over a
   218	distribution of the outcome sums of `Re ⟨u, A v⟩` is bounded by the product of
   219	the square roots of the two averaged diagonal sums. -/
   220	theorem abs_avgOver_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   221	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → α → Op ι)
   222	    (hA : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ A x a) (u v : X → α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   223	    |avgOver μ (fun x =>
   224	        ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re)| ≤
   225	      Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   226	          ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (u x a))).re)) *
   227	        Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   228	          ∑ a, (inner ℂ (v x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re)) := by
   229	  set f : X → ℝ := fun x =>
   230	    ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re with hf
   231	  set g : X → ℝ := fun x =>
   232	    ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (u x a))).re with hg
   233	  set h : X → ℝ := fun x =>
   234	    ∑ a, (inner ℂ (v x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re with hh
   235	  have hg0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x := fun x =>
   236	    Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => stateQForm_nonneg (u x a) (hA x a)
   237	  have hh0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ h x := fun x =>
   238	    Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => stateQForm_nonneg (v x a) (hA x a)
   239	  have hpoint : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ Real.sqrt (g x) * Real.sqrt (h x) := fun x =>
   240	    abs_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt (A x) (hA x) (u x) (v x)
   241	  unfold avgOver
   242	  calc
   243	    |∑ x ∈ μ.support, μ.weight x * f x|
   244	        ≤ ∑ x ∈ μ.support, |μ.weight x * f x| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   245	    _ = ∑ x ∈ μ.support, μ.weight x * |f x| := by
   246	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
   247	      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x)]
   248	    _ ≤ ∑ x ∈ μ.support, μ.weight x * (Real.sqrt (g x) * Real.sqrt (h x)) :=
   249	      Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ =>
   250	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hpoint x) (μ.nonnegative x)
   251	    _ = ∑ x ∈ μ.support,
   252	          Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * g x) * Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * h x) := by
   253	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
   254	      rw [Real.sqrt_mul (μ.nonnegative x), Real.sqrt_mul (μ.nonnegative x),
   255	        show Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) * Real.sqrt (g x) *
   256	            (Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) * Real.sqrt (h x)) =
   257	          Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) * Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) *
   258	            (Real.sqrt (g x) * Real.sqrt (h x)) by ring,
   259	        Real.mul_self_sqrt (μ.nonnegative x)]
   260	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ x ∈ μ.support, Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * g x) ^ 2) *
   261	          Real.sqrt (∑ x ∈ μ.support, Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * h x) ^ 2) :=
   262	      Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt _ _ _
   263	    _ = _ := by
   264	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ =>
   265	          Real.sq_sqrt (mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x) (hg0 x)),
   266	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ =>
   267	          Real.sq_sqrt (mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x) (hh0 x))]

   269	/-! ## Quadratic forms against projections -/
   270	
   271	/-- The real quadratic form is invariant under the conjugate transpose. -/
   272	theorem stateQForm_conjTranspose {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   273	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (M : Op ι) :
   274	    stateQForm ψ Mᴴ = stateQForm ψ M := by
   275	  unfold stateQForm
   276	  change (inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Mᴴ ψ)).re =
   277	    (inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ)).re
   278	  rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right,
   279	    ← inner_conj_symm, Complex.conj_re]
   280	
   281	/-- Conjugating an operator transfers the outer operator to the state vector. -/
   282	theorem stateQForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   283	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (W M : Op ι) :
   284	    stateQForm ψ (Wᴴ * M * W) = stateQForm (applyOperatorToState W ψ) M := by
   285	  unfold stateQForm
   286	  rw [applyOperatorToState_mul, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   287	  congr 1
   288	  change inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Wᴴ _) =
   289	    inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin W ψ) _
   290	  rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
   291	
   292	/-- For a projection `B` commuting with `A`, the quadratic form of `A` in
   293	`B ψ` is the quadratic form of `A B` in `ψ`. -/
   294	theorem stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   295	    [DecidableEq ι] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) {A B : Op ι} (hB : IsProj B)
   296	    (hAB : Commute A B) :
   297	    stateQForm (applyOperatorToState B ψ) A = stateQForm ψ (A * B) := by
   298	  rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul, hB.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
   299	    ← hAB.eq, mul_assoc, hB.isIdempotentElem.eq]
   300	
   301	/-- The quadratic form of an operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
   302	the squared norm of the vector. -/
   303	theorem stateQForm_le_norm_sq_of_le_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   304	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) {A : Op ι} (hA : A ≤ 1) :
   305	    stateQForm v A ≤ ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
   306	  rw [← stateQForm_one]
   307	  exact quadratic_form_mono hA v
   308	
   309	/-- The effects of a complete measurement have total quadratic form one on a
   310	unit vector. -/
   311	theorem sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι]
   312	    [DecidableEq ι] (A : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   313	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
   314	    (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a)) = 1 := by
   315	  calc
   316	    (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a)) =
   317	        stateQForm ψ (∑ a : α, A.effect a) := by
   318	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
   319	    _ = stateQForm ψ 1 := by rw [A.sum_eq_one]
   320	    _ = 1 := by rw [stateQForm_one, hψ, one_pow]
   321	
   322	/-- Weighting a complete measurement by commuting projections cannot exceed
   323	the total mass one. -/
   324	theorem avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   325	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
   326	    (C : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   327	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hC : ∀ x a, IsProj (C x a))
   328	    (hAC : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (C x a)) :
   329	    avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤ 1 := by
   330	  have hpt : ∀ x, (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤ 1 := by
   331	    intro x
   332	    calc
   333	      (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤
   334	          ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a) := by
   335	        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
   336	        have h1 : stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - C x a)) =
   337	            stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a) -
   338	              stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a) := by
   339	          simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   340	        have h2 : 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - C x a)) := by
   341	          rw [← stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj ψ (hC x a).one_sub
   342	            ((Commute.one_right _).sub_right (hAC x a))]
   343	          exact stateQForm_nonneg _ ((A x).pos a)
   344	        linarith
   345	      _ = 1 := sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one (A x) ψ hψ
   346	  calc
   347	    avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤
   348	        avgOver μ (fun _ => 1) := avgOver_mono μ _ _ hpt
   349	    _ = 1 := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ 1

   351	/-! ## Replacing a factor under the weight of a measurement -/
   352	
   353	/-- Cauchy--Schwarz with the measurement as weight: for projections `B`
   354	commuting with the effects of `A`, the averaged overlap of `A` against the
   355	product `B C` is bounded by the square roots of the averaged overlap of `A`
   356	against `B` and of the averaged quadratic form of `A` in `C ψ`.  This is the
   357	Cauchy--Schwarz step of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`,
   358	paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
   359	theorem abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {X α ι : Type*}
   360	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X)
   361	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B C : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   362	    (hB : ∀ x a, IsProj (B x a))
   363	    (hAB : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (B x a)) :
   364	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a * C x a)))| ≤
   365	      Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a))) *
   366	        Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a,
   367	          stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a))) := by
   368	  have hrw : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a * C x a)) =
   369	      (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   370	        (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a)
   371	          (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ))).re := by
   372	    intro x a
   373	    unfold stateQForm
   374	    rw [← mul_assoc, (hAB x a).eq, mul_assoc, applyOperatorToState_mul,
   375	      applyOperatorToState_mul]
   376	    congr 1
   377	    have hadj : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (B x a)).adjoint =
   378	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin (B x a) := by
   379	      rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint,
   380	        (hB x a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   381	    have h := LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (B x a)) ψ
   382	      (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a) (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ))
   383	    rw [hadj] at h
   384	    exact h
   385	  have hleft : (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) =
   386	      fun x => ∑ a, (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   387	        (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a)
   388	          (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ))).re :=
   389	    funext fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ =>
   390	      (stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj ψ (hB x a) (hAB x a)).symm
   391	  have hmain : (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a * C x a))) =
   392	      fun x => ∑ a, (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   393	        (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a)
   394	          (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ))).re :=
   395	    funext fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hrw x a
   396	  rw [hmain, hleft]
   397	  exact abs_avgOver_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
   398	    (fun x a => (A x).pos a) (fun x a => applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   399	    (fun x a => applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ)
   400	
   401	/-- Deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate: for projections `B` and `C`
   402	commuting with the effects of `A`, replacing the factor `C B` by `C` inside an
   403	overlap weighted by the complete measurement `A` changes the average by at
   404	most the square root of the deficit `1 - E Σ_a ⟨A_a B_a⟩`.  This is the
   405	estimate used in the proof of `lem:claim-17-2` and, with `C = Id`, in the proof
   406	of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
   407	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
   408	theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_one_sub_of_isProj {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   409	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
   410	    (B C : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   411	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hB : ∀ x a, IsProj (B x a)) (hC : ∀ x a, IsProj (C x a))
   412	    (hAB : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (B x a))
   413	    (hAC : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (C x a)) :
   414	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (C x a * B x a))) -
   415	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))| ≤
   416	      Real.sqrt (1 - avgOver μ (fun x =>
   417	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a))) := by
   418	  have hpt : ∀ x, (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) -
   419	      (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (C x a * B x a))) =
   420	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (C x a * (1 - B x a))) := by
   421	    intro x
   422	    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   423	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   424	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   425	  rw [abs_sub_comm, ← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
   426	  have h1B : ∀ x a, IsProj (1 - B x a) := fun x a => (hB x a).one_sub
   427	  have hA1B : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (1 - B x a) := fun x a =>
   428	    (Commute.one_right _).sub_right (hAB x a)
   429	  have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt μ A C
   430	    (fun x a => 1 - B x a) ψ hC hAC

     8	# A uniform point of the extended space from the directly indexed sub-line law
     9	
    10	The first scalar estimate in the combining argument samples an extended line
    11	from the auxiliary `SubLineWitness` and then a uniform affine parameter on that line.
    12	This module records that the resulting extended point is uniform and hence
    13	that its two source coordinate blocks are independent uniform points. These
    14	identities concern `directLinePointDist`. Transport to the source's seed-indexed
    15	carrier remains open, as recorded in
    16	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
    17	"Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law".
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	These statements support `lem:claim-17-1` in
    22	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  The paper uses this sampling
    23	fact at
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1159-1166`.
    25	-/

    35	/-- A dependent mixture of a constant family is the constant law. -/
    36	private theorem Distribution.bind_const_current {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    37	    (μ : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (ν : Distribution β) :
    38	    Distribution.bind μ (fun _ => ν) = ν := by
    39	  have hne : μ.support.Nonempty := by
    40	    rw [← Finset.card_pos]
    41	    by_contra hcard
    42	    have hempty : μ.support = ∅ := by
    43	      rw [← Finset.card_eq_zero]
    44	      omega
    45	    have htotal := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
    46	    rw [hempty] at htotal
    47	    simp at htotal
    48	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    49	  · change μ.support.biUnion (fun _ => ν.support) = ν.support
    50	    ext b
    51	    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion]
    52	    constructor
    53	    · rintro ⟨a, -, hb⟩
    54	      exact hb
    55	    · intro hb
    56	      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
    57	      exact ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
    58	  · funext b
    59	    change (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b) = ν.weight b
    60	    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hμ.weight_sum_eq_one, one_mul]
    61	
    62	/-- If every slice of a map of a pair carries the second uniform law to one
    63	fixed law, then the map carries the uniform law of the pair to that law. -/
    64	theorem uniformDistribution_map_uncurry {α β γ : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    66	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
    67	    (g : α × β → γ) (ν : Distribution γ)
    68	    (hg : ∀ a, (uniformDistribution β).map (fun b => g (a, b)) = ν) :
    69	    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map g = ν := by
    70	  rw [← bind_uniformDistribution_map (fun a b => g (a, b)),
    71	    show (fun a => (uniformDistribution β).map (fun b => g (a, b))) =
    72	      fun _ => ν from funext hg]
    73	  exact Distribution.bind_const_current _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability α) ν

    75	/-- Apply the shared uniform-point identity to an ambient point and an
    76	independent affine parameter. This preserves the existing public name for the
    77	identity supplied by `uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul`. -/
    78	theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul_current
    79	    {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    80	    (v : Fin m → K) :
    81	    (uniformDistribution ((Fin m → K) × K)).map
    82	        (fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) =
    83	      uniformDistribution (Fin m → K) := by
    84	  exact uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul v

    86	/-- Reading a point at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line of a
    87	uniform direct sample gives a uniform point of the direct coordinate space. -/
    88	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directLine_add_smul (D : DirectLdParams)
    89	    (V : Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :
    90	    (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map
    91	        (fun p => lineRepMap (V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) p.1.point +
    92	          p.2 • V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) =
    93	      uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) := by
    94	  classical
    95	  let e : DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D ≃
    96	      (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) ×
    97	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × DirectScalarQ D) :=
    98	    { toFun := fun p => ((p.1.index, p.1.direction), (p.1.point, p.2))
    99	      invFun := fun w => (⟨w.2.1, w.1.1, w.1.2⟩, w.2.2)
   100	      left_inv := by rintro ⟨⟨pt, i, dir⟩, t⟩; rfl
   101	      right_inv := by rintro ⟨⟨i, dir⟩, pt, t⟩; rfl }
   102	  have hequiv :
   103	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map e =
   104	        uniformDistribution ((Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) ×
   105	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   106	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv e
   107	  have hmap :
   108	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map
   109	          (fun p => lineRepMap (V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) p.1.point +
   110	            p.2 • V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) =
   111	        ((uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map e).map
   112	          (fun w => lineRepMap (V w.1) w.2.1 + w.2.2 • V w.1) := by
   113	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   114	    rfl
   115	  rw [hmap, hequiv]
   116	  refine uniformDistribution_map_uncurry _ _ fun a => ?_
   117	  exact uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul_current (V a)

   119	/-- Averaging a function at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line
   120	of a uniform direct sample is averaging it at a uniform point. -/
   121	theorem avgOver_uniform_directLdSpace_line_add_smul (D : DirectLdParams)
   122	    (V : Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   123	    (g : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → ℝ) :
   124	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)) (fun s =>
   125	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ D)) (fun t =>
   126	          g (lineRepMap (V (s.index, s.direction)) s.point +
   127	            t • V (s.index, s.direction)))) =
   128	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) g := by
   129	  classical
   130	  rw [← avgOver_uniform_prod]
   131	  calc
   132	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D))
   133	          (fun p => g (lineRepMap (V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) p.1.point +
   134	            p.2 • V (p.1.index, p.1.direction))) =
   135	        avgOver ((uniformDistribution
   136	            (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map
   137	          (fun p => lineRepMap (V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) p.1.point +
   138	            p.2 • V (p.1.index, p.1.direction))) g :=
   139	      (Distribution.avgOver_map _ _ g).symm
   140	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) g := by
   141	      rw [uniformDistribution_map_directLine_add_smul]

   145	theorem avgOver_directLinePointDist_line_add_smul (D : DirectLdParams)

   158	    exact avgOver_uniform_directLdSpace_line_add_smul D

   172	/-- Identify the directly indexed extended coordinates with the combining
   173	coordinate split. -/
   174	private def extendedFinCombineEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   175	    Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m ≃ ((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
   176	  (finCongr (by rfl)).trans (finCombineEquiv P.m)
   177	
   178	/-- Split an extended point into its two source blocks and two remaining
   179	scalar coordinates. -/
   180	private noncomputable def extendedPointBlocksEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   181	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
   182	      ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) ×
   183	        (Fin 2 → PauliScalar P) :=
   184	  (Equiv.arrowCongr (extendedFinCombineEquiv P)
   185	      (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P)).trans
   186	    ((Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow (Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) (Fin 2)
   187	      (PauliScalar P)).trans
   188	      (Equiv.prodCongr
   189	        (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow (Fin P.m) (Fin P.m) (PauliScalar P))
   190	        (Equiv.refl (Fin 2 → PauliScalar P))))

   192	/-- The two source blocks of a uniform extended point are independent and
   193	uniform after the canonical scalar identification. -/
   194	private theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ_pauli_current
   195	    (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   196	    (uniformDistribution
   197	          (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   198	        (fun u => (projX (directPointToPauli P u),
   199	          projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   200	      uniformDistribution
   201	        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   202	  classical
   203	  apply uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv (extendedPointBlocksEquiv P)
   204	  intro u
   205	  apply Prod.ext <;> funext i <;> rfl

   207	/-- Under a sub-line witness, the two source blocks of the point at a uniform
   208	affine parameter are independent uniform source points. -/
   209	theorem SubLineWitness.avgOver_projX_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams)
   210	    (sublines : SubLineWitness P)
   211	    (f : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) → ℝ) :
   212	    avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
   213	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   214	          (fun t =>
   215	            f (projX (directPointToPauli P
   216	                (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction)),
   217	              projZ (directPointToPauli P
   218	                (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) =
   219	      avgOver (uniformDistribution
   220	        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) f := by
   221	  classical
   222	  have hmarginal :
   223	      avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
   224	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   225	            (fun t => f (projX (directPointToPauli P
   226	                (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction)),
   227	              projZ (directPointToPauli P
   228	                (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) =
   229	        avgOver ((directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst)
   230	          (fun line =>
   231	            avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   232	              (fun t => f (projX (directPointToPauli P
   233	                  (line.base + t • line.direction)),
   234	                projZ (directPointToPauli P
   235	                  (line.base + t • line.direction))))) := by
   236	    rw [← sublines.extended_marginal, Distribution.avgOver_map]
   237	  refine hmarginal.trans ?_
   238	  refine (avgOver_directLinePointDist_line_add_smul P.extendedDirectLd
   239	    (fun u => f (projX (directPointToPauli P u),
   240	      projZ (directPointToPauli P u)))).trans ?_
   241	  rw [← uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ_pauli_current,
   242	    Distribution.avgOver_map]

    63	/-- A product-distribution average is the corresponding iterated average. -/
    64	private theorem avgOver_prod_current {α β : Type*}
    65	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    66	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (f : α × β → ℝ) :
    67	    avgOver (Distribution.prod μ ν) f =
    68	      avgOver μ (fun a => avgOver ν (fun b => f (a, b))) := by
    69	  classical
    70	  unfold avgOver

    72	    μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2 * f p) = _
    73	  rw [Finset.sum_product]
    74	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    75	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    76	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => by ring

   117	private theorem rpow_quarter_nonneg (x : ℝ) : 0 ≤ Real.rpow x (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   118	  change 0 ≤ x ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)
   119	  rcases lt_or_ge x 0 with hx | hx
   120	  · rw [Real.rpow_def_of_neg hx,
   121	      show (1 / 4 : ℝ) * Real.pi = Real.pi / 4 by ring, Real.cos_pi_div_four]
   122	    positivity
   123	  · exact Real.rpow_nonneg hx _

   125	private theorem sqrt_deficit_bound_le (m δP δQ : ℝ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hP : 0 ≤ δP)
   126	    (hQ : 0 ≤ δQ) :
   127	    Real.sqrt (2 * Real.sqrt (4 * m ^ 2 * δP) + 2 * Real.sqrt (4 * δQ)) ≤
   128	      2 * Real.sqrt m * (Real.rpow δP (1 / 4 : ℝ) + Real.rpow δQ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) := by
   129	  have hm0 : 0 ≤ m := by linarith
   130	  have hsqrtm : 1 ≤ Real.sqrt m := by
   131	    rw [← Real.sqrt_one]
   132	    exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hm
   133	  have h1 : Real.sqrt (4 * m ^ 2 * δP) = 2 * m * Real.sqrt δP := by
   134	    rw [Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity), show (4 * m ^ 2 : ℝ) = (2 * m) ^ 2 by ring,
   135	      Real.sqrt_sq (by linarith)]
   136	  have h2 : Real.sqrt (4 * δQ) = 2 * Real.sqrt δQ := by
   137	    rw [Real.sqrt_mul (by norm_num), show (4 : ℝ) = 2 ^ 2 by norm_num,
   138	      Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)]
   139	  have hquarter : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 ≤ x →
   140	      Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt x) = Real.rpow x (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   141	    intro x hx
   142	    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, ← Real.rpow_mul hx]
   143	    norm_num
   144	  have hsplit : ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b →
   145	      Real.sqrt (a + b) ≤ Real.sqrt a + Real.sqrt b := by
   146	    intro a b ha hb
   147	    rw [← Real.sqrt_sq (add_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg a) (Real.sqrt_nonneg b))]
   148	    refine Real.sqrt_le_sqrt ?_
   149	    nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt ha, Real.sq_sqrt hb, Real.sqrt_nonneg a,
   150	      Real.sqrt_nonneg b]
   151	  have hPa : 0 ≤ 2 * (2 * m * Real.sqrt δP) :=
   152	    mul_nonneg (by norm_num)
   153	      (mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) hm0) (Real.sqrt_nonneg _))
   154	  have hQa : 0 ≤ 2 * (2 * Real.sqrt δQ) :=
   155	    mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (Real.sqrt_nonneg _))
   156	  have hPb : Real.sqrt (2 * (2 * m * Real.sqrt δP)) =
   157	      2 * Real.sqrt m * Real.rpow δP (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   158	    rw [show 2 * (2 * m * Real.sqrt δP) = 2 ^ 2 * m * Real.sqrt δP by ring,
   159	      Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity), Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ 2),
   160	      Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2), hquarter δP hP]
   161	  have hQb : Real.sqrt (2 * (2 * Real.sqrt δQ)) = 2 * Real.rpow δQ (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   162	    rw [show 2 * (2 * Real.sqrt δQ) = 2 ^ 2 * Real.sqrt δQ by ring,
   163	      Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ 2),
   164	      Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2), hquarter δQ hQ]
   165	  rw [h1, h2]
   166	  calc
   167	    Real.sqrt (2 * (2 * m * Real.sqrt δP) + 2 * (2 * Real.sqrt δQ))
   168	        ≤ Real.sqrt (2 * (2 * m * Real.sqrt δP)) +
   169	          Real.sqrt (2 * (2 * Real.sqrt δQ)) := hsplit _ _ hPa hQa
   170	    _ = 2 * Real.sqrt m * Real.rpow δP (1 / 4 : ℝ) +
   171	          2 * Real.rpow δQ (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by rw [hPb, hQb]
   172	    _ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt m *
   173	          (Real.rpow δP (1 / 4 : ℝ) + Real.rpow δQ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) := by
   174	      have hQ4 : 0 ≤ Real.rpow δQ (1 / 4 : ℝ) := Real.rpow_nonneg hQ _
   175	      nlinarith [hsqrtm, hQ4]

   177	/-- Regroup paired-line answers by their two optional evaluations. -/
   178	private theorem regroup_placed_line_answer_sum {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
   179	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
   180	    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
   181	    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   182	    (G : Option (PauliScalar P) → Option (PauliScalar P) →
   183	      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
   184	    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   185	        stateQForm S.psiHat
   186	          (((placedAAMeasurement S (lines.T .alice lineX lineZ)).postprocess
   187	            (fun fs => (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))).effect o *
   188	            S.place .BA'' (G o.1 o.2))) =
   189	      ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
   190	        (S.place .AA' ((lines.T .alice lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ)) *
   191	          S.place .BA'' (G (evalOpt lineX x fX) (evalOpt lineZ z fZ))) := by
   192	  classical
   193	  have hsum : ∀ (s : Finset (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   194	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)))
   195	      (M : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   196	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
   197	        Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB))
   198	      (N : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)),
   199	      stateQForm S.psiHat ((∑ fs ∈ s, M fs) * N) =
   200	        ∑ fs ∈ s, stateQForm S.psiHat (M fs * N) := by
   201	    intro s M N
   202	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, Finset.sum_mul]
   203	  calc
   204	    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   205	          stateQForm S.psiHat
   206	            (((placedAAMeasurement S
   207	              (lines.T .alice lineX lineZ)).postprocess (fun fs =>
   208	                (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))).effect o *
   209	              S.place .BA'' (G o.1 o.2))) =
   210	        ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   211	          ∑ fs ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun fs =>
   212	              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2) = o),

    46	/-- A seed-bearing line description for blueprint
    47	`def:line-point-dist`, paper
    48	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
    49	
    50	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    51	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    52	Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
    54	corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Multivariate polynomials in `m` variables whose total degree is at most
   110	`d`. This is the class `deg_d` in blueprint
   111	`def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
   112	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-52`. -/
   113	abbrev TotalDegreePoly (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :=
   114	  {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K // p.totalDegree ≤ d}
   115	
   116	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   117	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   118	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   119	
   120	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   121	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   122	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   123	  fun i =>
   124	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   125	
   126	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   127	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   128	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   129	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   130	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   131	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   132	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   133	
   134	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   135	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   136	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   138	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   139	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   140	  classical
   141	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   142	    some (Classical.choose h)
   143	  else none
   144	
   145	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   147	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   151	
   152	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   153	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   154	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   156	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   157	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   158	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   159	      intro j hj
   160	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   161	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   162	
   163	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   164	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   165	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   171	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   172	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   173	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   174	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   175	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   176	
   177	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   178	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   179	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   180	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   181	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   182	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   183	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   184	
   185	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   186	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   187	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability :=
   188	  ((uniformDistribution_isProbability _).map _).map _
   189	
   190	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   191	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   192	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability :=
   193	  ((uniformDistribution_isProbability _).map _).map _
   194	
   195	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   196	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   197	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   198	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   199	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   200	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
    95	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    96	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    97	
    98	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   100	-/
   101	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   102	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   103	
   104	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   106	-/
   107	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   108	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   109	
   110	/-- The zero-based coordinate index corresponding to the paper's map `χ`:
   111	`chiIndex P s` represents `χ(s) - 1` in the fixed field representation.  This
   112	is `eq:chi-func` in blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`, paper origin
   113	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   114	-/
   115	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   116	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   117	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   118	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   119	
   120	/-! ### Formalization-only coordinate-index fibers
   121	
   122	The following decomposition supplies the equal-fiber calculation used in the
   123	uniform coordinate-index law.
   124	-/
   125	
   126	/-- The common residue set in a fiber of `chiIndex` is nonempty.  This is part
   127	of the exact seed decomposition supporting the balance assertion in
   128	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `lem:chi-seed-fibers`, paper
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:215-221`.
   130	-/
   131	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   132	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   133	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   134	    rw [hq]
   135	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm

     5	/-!
     6	# The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
     7	
     8	This module carries out the sampling procedure of `lem:qld-sublines`.  A line
     9	kind is drawn from the two kinds, an extended coordinate and an extended point
    10	and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn
    11	independently in the coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates that the
    12	two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
    13	diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
    14	decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
    15	from the two seeds.
    16	
    17	The module records the elementary evaluations of that triple, the description
    18	of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a
    19	sampled triple -- incidence of the two source blocks, compatibility of the
    20	affine data, and closure of the axis branch -- and the identification of its
    21	extended-line marginal.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The construction is the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    26	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    28	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    29	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    30	-/

    41	
    42	/-- An extended point together with an extended direction.  Blueprint
    43	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    45	abbrev SubLinePointDir (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    46	  (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
    47	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
    48	
    49	/-- The auxiliary randomness of one branch of the sampling procedure: an
    50	extended point, an extended direction, and the two scalar seeds of the two
    51	source lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    53	abbrev SubLineRaw (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    54	  SubLinePointDir P × (ScalarQ P.toLdParams × ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
    55	
    56	/-- The law of the scalar seed carried by a source line at a given coordinate
    57	index: uniform on the coordinate-index fiber of that index.  Blueprint
    58	`def:ith-restricted-line`, paper
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
    60	noncomputable def subLineSeedDist (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
    61	    Distribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams) :=
    62	  Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams))
    63	    (ldSeedIndexEvent P.toLdParams i) (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
    64	
    65	/-- Every seed law of a source line has total mass one. -/
    66	theorem subLineSeedDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
    67	    (subLineSeedDist P i).IsProbability := by
    68	  rw [subLineSeedDist]
    69	  exact Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    70	    (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
    71	
    72	/-- The auxiliary randomness law of the sampling procedure: the extended
    73	coordinate is uniform, the extended point and direction are uniform and
    74	independent of it, and the two seeds are independent and uniform on the
    75	coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates carried by the two source
    76	lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    78	noncomputable def subLineRawDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    79	    Distribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLineRaw P) :=
    80	  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
    81	    (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    82	        (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    83	          (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map fun w => (k, w)
    84	
    85	/-- The auxiliary randomness law has total mass one. -/
    86	theorem subLineRawDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (subLineRawDist P).IsProbability := by
    88	  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
    89	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun k _ => ?_
    90	  exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
    91	    (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)
    92	      (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _)
    93	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _))) _

    97	/-- The extended line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line of an
