     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.UniformLinePoint
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Sub-line averages of the Z-point overlap
     6	
     7	The overlap of the paired-line measurement with the expanded `Z`-point effect
     8	depends only on the two source lines and the `Z`-point. The separate Z marginal
     9	of the auxiliary `SubLineWitness` law is a mixture of products of restricted
    10	line-point laws, with the fresh X point unused. Summing line answers over the
    11	evaluation fibers at that fresh point identifies the overlap with the
    12	evaluated pair-line overlap, so the Z deficit estimates of
    13	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.ZEvalDeficit` apply component by component.
    14	
    15	The `_at` estimates and `zPointOverlapAt` retain arbitrary
    16	opposite placements. The original overlap definitions and first-player
    17	statements are unchanged. Only the separate Z marginal mixture law is used.
    18	Transport of the auxiliary extended-line law to the source carrier remains
    19	open; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
    20	"Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law".
    21	
    22	## References
    23	
    24	The statements support the auxiliary `lem:claim-17-3-direct-real`, near
    25	the source `lem:claim-17-3` in
    26	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
    28	mixture is Property~2 of `lem:qld-sublines`.
    29	-/
    30	
    31	open scoped BigOperators
    32	
    33	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    34	
    35	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus
    36	
    37	noncomputable section
    38	
    39	/-! ## Regrouping the line answers by their evaluations -/
    40	
    41	/-- Summing a paired-line answer against a family of point effects that
    42	depends on the answer only through its two evaluations is summing the
    43	evaluation classes of the paired-line measurement against that family.  This
    44	is the fiber regrouping of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-1`, `lem:claim-17-2`,
    45	and `lem:claim-17-3` in the blueprint. -/
    46	theorem regroup_line_answer_sum_at {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
    47	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
    48	    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    49	    (first second : Placement)
    50	    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    51	    (G : Option (PauliScalar P) → Option (PauliScalar P) →
    52	      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace second.side)) :
    53	    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
    54	        stateQForm S.psiHat
    55	          ((S.placedMeasurement first
    56	            ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).postprocess (fun fs =>
    57	              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2)))).effect o *
    58	            S.place second (G o.1 o.2))) =
    59	      ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
    60	        (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ)) *
    61	          S.place second (G (evalOpt lineX x fX) (evalOpt lineZ z fZ))) := by
    62	  classical
    63	  have hsum : ∀ (s : Finset (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
    64	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)))
    65	      (M : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
    66	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
    67	        Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace first.side))
    68	      (N : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)),
    69	      stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place first (∑ fs ∈ s, M fs) * N) =
    70	        ∑ fs ∈ s, stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place first (M fs) * N) := by
    71	    intro s M N
    72	    rw [S.place_finsetSum]
    73	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, Finset.sum_mul]
    74	  calc
    75	    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
    76	          stateQForm S.psiHat
    77	            ((S.placedMeasurement first
    78	              ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).postprocess (fun fs =>
    79	                (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2)))).effect o *
    80	              S.place second (G o.1 o.2))) =
    81	        ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
    82	          ∑ fs ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun fs =>
    83	              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2) = o),
    84	            stateQForm S.psiHat
    85	              (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
    86	                S.place second (G o.1 o.2)) := by
    87	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun o _ => ?_
    88	      rw [ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect,
    89	        MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
    90	      exact hsum _ _ _
    91	    _ = ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
    92	          ∑ fs ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun fs =>
    93	              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2) = o),
    94	            stateQForm S.psiHat
    95	              (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
    96	                S.place second
    97	                  (G (evalOpt lineX x fs.1) (evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))) := by
    98	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun o _ =>
    99	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun fs hfs => ?_
   100	      rw [← (Finset.mem_filter.mp hfs).2]
   101	    _ = ∑ fs : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   102	          DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d),
   103	          stateQForm S.psiHat
   104	            (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
   105	              S.place second
   106	                (G (evalOpt lineX x fs.1) (evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))) :=
   107	      Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to (fun fs _ => Finset.mem_univ _) _
   108	    _ = ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
   109	          (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ)) *
   110	            S.place second (G (evalOpt lineX x fX) (evalOpt lineZ z fZ))) :=
   111	      Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := fun fs => stateQForm S.psiHat
   112	        (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
   113	          S.place second (G (evalOpt lineX x fs.1) (evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))))

   115	theorem regroup_line_answer_sum {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
   116	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
   117	    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
   118	    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   119	    (G : Option (PauliScalar P) → Option (PauliScalar P) →
   120	      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
   121	    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   122	        stateQForm S.psiHat
   123	          ((S.placedMeasurement .AA'
   124	            ((lines.T .alice lineX lineZ).postprocess (fun fs =>
   125	              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2)))).effect o *
   126	            S.place .BA'' (G o.1 o.2))) =

   133	`Z`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products

   140	    (F : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   141	      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → ℝ) :
   142	    ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P), components.IsProbability ∧

   144	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   145	            (fun t => F (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
   146	              (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) =
   147	        avgOver components (fun c =>
   148	          avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)
   149	              (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
   150	            (fun w => F ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2))) := by
   151	  obtain ⟨components, hcomp, -, hZ⟩ := sublines.source_mixture
   152	  refine ⟨components, hcomp, ?_⟩
   153	  have h1 : avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
   154	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   155	        (fun t => F (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P

   157	      avgOver ((subLinePointDist P sublines.D).map subLineZProjection) F := by
   158	    rw [Distribution.avgOver_map, subLinePointDist, Distribution.avgOver_map,
   159	      avgOver_prod]
   160	    rfl
   161	  rw [h1, hZ, avgOver_bind]
   162	  refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun c => ?_
   163	  rw [subLineZComponentDist, Distribution.avgOver_map, Distribution.prod_map_left,

   167	
   168	section Overlaps
   169	
   170	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
   171	  {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
   172	
   173	/-- The overlap of the paired-line measurement at two source lines with the
   174	expanded `Z`-point effect at a point, summed over the line answers.  This is

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
   196	
   197	[#1145]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/1145

1	# Blueprint Style Guide & Lessons Learned
     2	
     3	## Core Philosophy
     4	The blueprint is a **bridge between the mathematics and the Lean formalization**. A reader should be able to read a blueprint entry and immediately understand the corresponding Lean declaration. Conversely, someone reading the Lean code should find the blueprint proof sketch faithful to what the code actually does.
     5	
     6	## General Principles
     7	1. **Blueprint ↔ Lean must match.** Every `\lean{X}` tag must correspond to an actual Lean declaration. Every proof sketch must match what the Lean proof actually does — not a hand-wavy version of it.
     8	2. **Standalone.** `blueprint/` and any slides are independent — no cross-references, no shared files. Each has its own macros, its own `references.bib`.
     9	3. **Mathematical language only — zero Lean jargon.** No Lean identifiers in prose (no `selfImprovement_step`, no `PastingLemma.aux`, no `rintro ⟨X, hX⟩`). The `\lean{...}` tag is the link; the body text is standard mathematics. If you can't say it in math, rewrite it.
    10	4. **No filler prose.** Only precise definitions, theorem statements, and proof sketches. No "this is important because..." or "the self-improvement step governs the induction...".
    11	5. **Cite non-trivial things.** Basic definitions don't need citations. Important results and non-obvious definitions should cite the source paper.
    12	6. **Don't invent terminology or notation.** Don't create ad-hoc notation when standard notation exists. Don't name things that the literature doesn't name.
    13	7. **Match Lean's theorem/lemma/def exactly.** If Lean says `theorem X`, use `\begin{theorem}`. If Lean says `lemma X`, use `\begin{lemma}`. `\begin{proposition}` is allowed in blueprint prose when it improves mathematical readability, but still map it to an actual Lean `theorem`/`lemma` declaration via `\lean{...}`. Label prefix: `thm:` for theorem, `lem:` for lemma, `def:` for definition, `prop:` for proposition.
    14	
    15	### Remark On Mathematical Prose
    16	
    17	Blueprint entries should read as mathematical exposition, not as progress
    18	reports. The mathematical argument should determine the order of the prose:
    19	introduce the notation, state the assertion, give the proof or calculation, and
    20	then record Lean references through the usual blueprint tags. Lean declarations,
    21	file paths, and proof-status information should not become the visible structure
    22	of the paragraph. When referring to a source article, cite it bibliographically
    23	rather than relying on an uncited reference to the article.
    24	
    25	Use displayed formulae when the formula benefits from visual separation, and
    26	keep short scalar definitions or elementary inequalities inline when the
    27	sentence reads better that way. As in ordinary mathematical writing, displayed
    28	formulae should be punctuated as part of the sentences in which they occur.
    29	
    30	## Proof Sketches Must Match Lean
    31	This is the most important rule. Every proof in the blueprint must faithfully describe what the Lean proof does:
    32	
    33	- **Reference the actual lemmas used.** If the Lean proof calls `LDT.selfImprovement`, the blueprint proof should say "By Lemma X.Y (self-improvement)..." and list it in `\uses`.
    34	- **Do not use `\cref` or `\Cref`.** The blueprint does not load `cleveref`.
    35	  Spell out the kind of object and use ordinary references, for example
    36	  `Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement}` or `Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal}`.
    37	- **Describe the actual proof structure.** If Lean does induction on a parameter, say so. If Lean uses a specific decomposition, name it.
    38	- **Don't hand-wave where Lean is specific.** "Standard argument" is not acceptable if Lean uses three specific lemmas. Name them.
    39	- **Don't be more specific than Lean.** If Lean uses `simp` to close a goal, a one-line sketch is fine.
    40	- **`\uses` in proofs must be accurate.** Only list what the proof actually uses, not what the statement mentions.
    41	
    42	## Source-Labelled Statements And Conditional Helpers
    43	
    44	If a blueprint theorem, lemma, or proposition carries a source label from the
    45	paper, the linked Lean declaration must state the same theorem, up to faithful
    46	formal encoding of the paper's domain.  Do not use `\lean{...}` and `\leanok`
    47	on the source-labelled statement to point to a conditional helper whose
    48	additional assumptions supply an unproved part of the paper proof.
    49	Changing the Lean statement away from `references/ldt-paper/` is strongly
    50	discouraged unless faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical
    51	necessity requires it; the blueprint should make any such necessity explicit.
    52	
    53	Boundary hypotheses such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
    54	positivity of parameters, and denominator nonvanishing may be faithful when
    55	they express the mathematical domain that the paper leaves implicit.  By
    56	contrast, bridge inputs, residual data, repair hypotheses, producer
    57	assumptions, proof-obligation inputs, or package assumptions are proof debt.
    58	They must not be added to a source-labelled theorem statement.  If such data is
    59	still unproved, the source-labelled Lean theorem should keep the source-shaped
    60	statement and carry a tracked `sorry`, or the missing assertion should appear
    61	as the lowest named internal obligation with a tracked `sorry`.  A separately
    62	named conditional helper should not be introduced as a repair pattern.  If one
    63	already contains substantial proof content, it may remain temporarily only as
    64	quarantine: it needs a paper source, a tracking issue, and a discharge or
    65	deletion plan.  The blueprint should leave the paper theorem unmarked as
    66	proof-complete until the source-faithful Lean statement has a source-faithful
    67	proof.
    68	
    69	If a Lean theorem proves only a restricted version of a source theorem, the
    70	blueprint entry carrying `\leanok` must state that restriction in the theorem
    71	statement itself.  It must not be cited as the unrestricted source theorem.
    72	When the only Lean declaration available for a source label has extra
    73	non-paper assumptions, remove the `\leanok` claim from the source-labelled
    74	entry or move the restricted statement to a separate Lean-only entry.  The
    75	unrestricted paper theorem remains unformalized until a Lean statement with
    76	the source's hypothesis set exists.
    77	
    78	## Notation Consistency
   126	### Additional rules:
   127	- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
   128	- **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
   129	- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.
   130	
   131	## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
   132	- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
   133	- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
   134	- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
   135	
   136	## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
   137	Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
   138	from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
   139	look as if the paper stated them.
   140	
   141	- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
   142	  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
   143	- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
   144	  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
   145	  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
   146	  anchored paper passage, or blueprint label it supports. Blueprint line
   147	  ranges are derived review context, not stored docstring citations; resolve a
   148	  label with `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve <label>`.
   149	- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
   150	  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
   151	  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
   152	  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
   153	  Lean proof.
   154	- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
   155	  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
   156	  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
   157	  used.
   158	- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
   159	  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
   160	  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
   161	  proof remains tracked as incomplete.
   162	
   163	## Blueprint Structure
   164	- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.
   165	- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`
   166	- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`
   167	
   168	## Lean Blueprint Macros
   169	- `\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration
   170	- `\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see "Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`" below
   171	- `\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph
   172	- `\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)
   173	- `\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)
   174	
   175	### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`
   176	
   177	`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.
   178	
   179	**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.
   180	
   181	**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).
   182	
   183	A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.
   184	
   185	Excerpt from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`:

Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:4:# Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:6:The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:7:the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:8:scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:9:coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:10:of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:11:This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:12:source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:13:reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:14:line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:15:same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:17:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:19:The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:20:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:21:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:22:The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:23:445--480, paper lines 970--989.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:24:-/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:7:The six-register state of `eq:def-psihat` factors as the two-player state
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:8:`ExtendedLineGame.pairState` and an unused normalized EPR pair, for each of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:9:the opposite register placements `AA'`--`BA''` and `AB''`--`BB'`. Therefore
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:10:arbitrary Hermitian operators on the expanded local spaces have the same
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:11:correlation in the two descriptions. An individual operator need not factor
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:12:between its strategy register and its Pauli register.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:14:These are formalization-only auxiliary identities for the strategy construction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:15:in the proof of `lem:qld-4-7`. They do not establish its passing value or the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/StateTransport.lean:16:existence of its input measurements. Parent issue #119 remains open.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:4:# Positivity of the consistency defect on opposite placements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:6:The error-inflation estimates for restricted line distributions apply to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:7:nonnegative averages.  This module supplies the missing nonnegativity: the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:8:integrand of `consistencyDefect` for two complete measurements placed on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:9:opposite registers is a state quadratic form of a positive operator.  Indeed,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:10:after separating the two placements along the corresponding tensor
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:11:bipartition, the off-diagonal sum is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:12:`∑_a (place p₁ E_a) (place p₂ (∑_{b ≠ a} F_b))`, a sum of products of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:13:positive operators supported on complementary registers.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:14:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:15:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:17:The consistency defect is blueprint `def:consistency`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:18:`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`.  The
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:19:placements and their bipartitions are blueprint `def:expanded-state`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.  The
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:21:nonnegativity is the hypothesis of items 1 and 2 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:22:blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:23:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:24:-/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:4:# Coordinate blocks of a truncated extended direction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:6:This module computes the two source blocks of the direction of an extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:7:diagonal line.  That direction is obtained from an unrestricted extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:8:vector by zeroing the coordinates that precede the stored coordinate index,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:9:so each source block is again a prefix truncation: when the stored index is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:10:the `i`-th coordinate of a block, that block inherits the truncation at `i`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:11:preceding blocks vanish, and later blocks remain untruncated.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:12:The computation is recorded after transport to the source scalar field, since
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:13:the extended direction and the source line directions are presented over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:14:two identified scalar fields.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:16:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:17:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:18:The block computations support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:19:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:21:The truncation is the prefix restriction of blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:22:`def:ld-question-distribution`; the coordinate blocks are those of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:23:blueprint `def:combine-map`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean:24:-/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:4:# The branch data of the sub-line sampling procedure
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:6:The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma draws a line kind, a stored
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:7:extended coordinate, and an unrestricted extended direction, and forms from
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:8:them the direction of the extended line: the elementary direction at the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:9:stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:10:coordinates preceding the stored coordinate replaced by zero in the diagonal
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:11:branch.  The two source lines are then read off the two coordinate blocks.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:12:This module fixes the coordinate index that each source line must carry: the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:13:stored coordinate itself when it belongs to that block, the first coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:14:otherwise.  With that choice the source block of the extended direction always
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:15:lies in the line spanned by the corresponding source direction, which is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:16:incidence hypothesis of the two projection lemmas.  The module also records
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:17:that moving an extended point to its canonical representative does not change
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:18:the canonical representative of either of its source blocks.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:19:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:20:## References

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:24:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:4:# The quantum linearity theorem
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:6:This file proves the quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick in the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:7:form used to combine the binary observables produced in the point analysis.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:8:A family of binary observables indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`, whose
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:9:two-query linearity correlation weighted by a positive semidefinite trace-one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:10:operator `ρ` is at least `1 - δ`, is close on average, in the state-dependent
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:11:distance weighted by `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, to an exactly linear family of binary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:12:observables on a finite ancillary extension.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:14:The proof assembles two results of the linearity route: the operator BLR bound
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:15:`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, which converts the correlation
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:16:hypothesis into the bound `2δ` on the average multiplicative defect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:17:`E_{u,u'} d_ρ(O^u O^{u'}, O^{u+u'})^2`, and Boolean representation stability
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:18:`exists_exact_boolean_representation`, which converts that defect bound into
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:19:the exactly linear family with the same average distance bound.  The notions
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:20:in which the theorem is stated are in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:21:`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:22:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:23:## Main results
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:24:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:25:* `exists_exactly_linear_observables`: the theorem, with the closeness measured
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:26:  by the squared state-dependent operator distance `stateDepDistSq` and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:27:  bound `2 * δ`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:28:* `exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq`: the same
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:29:  conclusion measured by the binary-measurement distance
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:30:  `binaryObservableDistSq`, with the bound `δ` intended by the source.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:31:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:32:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:33:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:34:The declaration is blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:35:`thm:linearity`.  The QPBT paper quotes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:36:the theorem at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:37:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:38:provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:39:`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`.  The normalization of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:40:distance bound is analyzed in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:41:`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:42:-/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:52:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:53:/-- The quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan--Vidick.  Let `t` be positive,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:54:`δ ≥ 0`, `ρ` a positive semidefinite trace-one operator on a finite-dimensional
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:55:Hilbert space, and `O^u`, for `u ∈ F_2^t`, binary observables whose two-query
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:56:correlation satisfies `E_{u,u'} Re Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ) ≥ 1 - δ`.  Then
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:57:there are a finite-dimensional ancillary Hilbert space, a unit vector `anc` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:58:it, and binary observables `L^u` on the tensor-product Hilbert space such that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:59:`L^u L^{u'} = L^{u+u'}` for all `u, u'` and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:60:`E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 ≤ 2δ`, where `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:61:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:62:This is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:63:`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`, hypothesis as in its display
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:64:(7) and conclusion as in its display (8), stated as blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:65:`thm:linearity`; the QPBT paper quotes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:66:it at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:67:As recorded in blueprint `rem:linearity-import`, this form
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:68:imposes no upper bound on `δ`, asserts exact linearity for every pair, and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:69:averages closeness only over `u`.  The quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:70:closeness pointwise under a pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:71:deviations are not reproduced.  The identity at zero follows from exact
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:72:linearity and the binary-observable condition.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:73:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:74:**Local fix:** The source prints the closeness bound as `δ` for the squared
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:75:state-dependent operator distance.  Its calculation at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:76:`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912` bounds the squared distance between
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:77:the binary projective measurements of the observables, which is half the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:78:squared operator distance, and then identifies the two quantities; the operator
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:79:bound `δ` is refuted by a four-point counterexample, and the bound established
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:80:by the Fourier--Naimark argument is `2 * δ` for `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:81:`δ` for `binaryObservableDistSq`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:82:(`exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq`).  Documented in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:83:`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex` and blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:84:`rem:linearity-distance-normalization`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:85:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:86:The proof passes the correlation hypothesis through the operator BLR bound
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:87:`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, obtaining
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:88:`E_{u,u'} d_ρ(O^u O^{u'}, O^{u+u'})^2 ≤ 2δ`, and applies Boolean representation
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:89:stability `exists_exact_boolean_representation` with `η = 2δ`. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:116:/-- The quantum linearity theorem with the closeness measured by the distance

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:148:              (fun u => binaryObservableDistSq (L u)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean:149:                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:1:import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineBranch
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:2:import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineProduct
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3:import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineSeed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:4:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:5:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:6:# The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:7:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:8:This module carries out the sampling procedure of `lem:qld-sublines`.  A line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:9:kind is drawn from the two kinds, an extended coordinate and an extended point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:10:and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:11:independently in the coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates that the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:12:two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:13:diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:14:decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:15:from the two seeds.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:17:The module records the elementary evaluations of that triple, the description
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:18:of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:19:sampled triple -- incidence of the two source blocks, compatibility of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:20:affine data, and closure of the axis branch -- and the identification of its
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:21:extended-line marginal.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:22:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:23:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:24:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:25:The construction is the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:26:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:27:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:28:The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:29:1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:30:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:31:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:32:open scoped BigOperators
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:33:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:34:namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:35:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:36:open MIPStarRE.LDT
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:37:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:38:noncomputable section
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:39:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:40:/-! ## The auxiliary randomness of one branch -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:41:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:42:/-- An extended point together with an extended direction.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:43:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:44:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:45:abbrev SubLinePointDir (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:46:  (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:47:    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:48:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:49:/-- The auxiliary randomness of one branch of the sampling procedure: an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:50:extended point, an extended direction, and the two scalar seeds of the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:51:source lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:52:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:53:abbrev SubLineRaw (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:54:  SubLinePointDir P × (ScalarQ P.toLdParams × ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:55:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:56:/-- The law of the scalar seed carried by a source line at a given coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:57:index: uniform on the coordinate-index fiber of that index.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:58:`def:ith-restricted-line`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:59:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:60:noncomputable def subLineSeedDist (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:61:    Distribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:62:  Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:63:    (ldSeedIndexEvent P.toLdParams i) (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:64:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:65:/-- Every seed law of a source line has total mass one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:66:theorem subLineSeedDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:67:    (subLineSeedDist P i).IsProbability := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:68:  rw [subLineSeedDist]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:69:  exact Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:70:    (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:71:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:72:/-- The auxiliary randomness law of the sampling procedure: the extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:73:coordinate is uniform, the extended point and direction are uniform and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:74:independent of it, and the two seeds are independent and uniform on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:75:coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates carried by the two source
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:76:lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:77:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:78:noncomputable def subLineRawDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:79:    Distribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLineRaw P) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:80:  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:81:    (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:82:        (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:83:          (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map fun w => (k, w)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:84:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:85:/-- The auxiliary randomness law has total mass one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:86:theorem subLineRawDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:87:    (subLineRawDist P).IsProbability := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:88:  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:89:    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun k _ => ?_
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:90:  exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:91:    (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:92:      (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:93:        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _))) _
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:94:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:95:/-! ## The sampled triple -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:96:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:97:/-- The extended line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line of an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:98:extended sample.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:99:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:100:noncomputable def subLineExtLineOfSample (P : AdmissibleParams)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:101:    (kind : LineKind) (s : DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:102:    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:103:  match kind with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:104:  | .axis => directALineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:105:  | .diagonal => directDLineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:106:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:107:/-- The extended line of a branch, read off the auxiliary randomness.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:108:Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:109:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:110:noncomputable def subLineExtLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:111:    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:112:    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:113:  subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:114:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:115:/-- A source line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line decoded
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:116:from a point block, a scalar seed and a direction block.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:117:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:118:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:119:noncomputable def subLineSourceLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:120:    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:121:    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : LineDesc P.toLdParams :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:122:  match kind with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:123:  | .axis => aLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:124:  | .diagonal => dLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:125:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:126:/-- The triple sampled by one branch of the procedure: the extended line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:127:together with the two source lines decoded from its two coordinate blocks and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:128:from the two scalar seeds.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:129:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:130:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:131:noncomputable def subLineTripleOf (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:132:    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) : SubLineTriple P :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:133:  (subLineExtLine P kind k w,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:134:    (subLineSourceLine P kind (projX (directPointToPauli P w.1.1)) w.2.1
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:135:        (projX (directPointToPauli P w.1.2)),
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:136:      subLineSourceLine P kind (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.1)) w.2.2
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:137:        (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.2))))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:138:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:139:/-- The law of the triples sampled by one branch.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:140:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:141:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:142:noncomputable def subLineBranchDist (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:143:    Distribution (SubLineTriple P) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:144:  (subLineRawDist P).map fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind w.1 w.2
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:145:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:146:/-- The sub-line law of `lem:qld-sublines`: the equal mixture of the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:147:branches of the sampling procedure.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:148:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:149:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:150:noncomputable def subLineDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:151:    Distribution (SubLineTriple P) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:152:  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin 2))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:153:    ![subLineBranchDist P .axis, subLineBranchDist P .diagonal]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:154:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:155:/-! ## Elementary evaluations of the sampled triple -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:156:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:157:/-- The extended line of a branch has the kind of that branch. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:158:theorem subLineExtLine_kind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:159:    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:160:    (subLineExtLine P kind k w).kind = kind := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:161:  cases kind <;> rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:162:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:163:/-- The direction of the extended line of a branch is the branch direction. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:164:theorem subLineExtLine_direction (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:165:    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:166:    (subLineExtLine P kind k w).direction =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:167:      subLineExtDirection P kind k w.1.2 := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:168:  cases kind <;> rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:169:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:170:/-- The base of the extended line of a branch is the canonical representative
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:171:of the drawn point in the branch direction. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:172:theorem subLineExtLine_base (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:173:    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:174:    (subLineExtLine P kind k w).base =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:175:      lineRepMap (subLineExtDirection P kind k w.1.2) w.1.1 := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:176:  cases kind <;> rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:177:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:178:/-- A source line of a branch has the kind of that branch. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:179:theorem subLineSourceLine_kind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:180:    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:181:    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:4:# The two independent blocks of a fresh diagonal direction pair
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:6:This module splits the fresh diagonal direction pair of the sub-line sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:7:procedure into its two independent blocks.  The coordinate-index event
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:8:constrains only the scalar seed of the pair, so conditioning on it leaves the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:9:direction block uniform and independent of the conditioned seed.  The
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:10:direction block of a fresh pair is therefore available as an unconstrained
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:11:uniform vector, which is what allows the sampling procedure to read it off the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:12:corresponding block of the direction of the sampled extended line.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:14:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:16:The block decomposition supports `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:17:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:18:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:19:The coordinate-index event is that of `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean:20:lines 1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:8:with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:12:triangle inequality twice.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:93:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:94:/-- The axis and diagonal line-point laws are uniform mixtures of their
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:95:coordinate-index restrictions.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:96:

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:104:theorem linePointDist_eq_mixture_restricted (L : LdParams) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:105:    aLinePointDist L =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:106:        Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:107:          (restrictedALineDist L) ∧

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:109:        Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:110:          (restrictedDLineDist L) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:111:  ⟨aLinePointDist_eq_bind_restricted L, dLinePointDist_eq_bind_restricted L⟩
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:112:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:113:/-- Restricting a nonnegative average from the line-point distribution to one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:114:fixed line kind and coordinate inflates its bound by at most `2m`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:115:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:116:**Source statement:** item 1 of blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:117:`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, from the unlabelled
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:118:estimate at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:119:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1056`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:120:The restricted component carries mixture weight `1 / (2m)`, so a nonnegative
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:121:average bounded by `δ` bounds it by `2mδ`. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:125:    (havg : avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f ≤ δ)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:126:    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:127:    avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i) f ≤

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:134:

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:238:its proof at lines 1071--1116.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:239:

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:242:line-point law of `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:243:place of the seed-indexed line-point distribution over `F_q^(2m+2)` of the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:247:conditional law.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:5:# Independent blocks of the restricted line-point laws
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:7:This module isolates the independent generating blocks of the restricted
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:8:line-point laws used by the sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma.  A
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:9:uniformly sampled low-degree vector splits into a point block and a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:10:seed-direction block; the coordinate-index event constrains only the second
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:11:block, so conditioning on it leaves the point block uniform and independent.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:12:The conditioned seed-direction block is the fresh diagonal direction pair of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:13:the sub-line construction, and the uniform mixture of those pairs over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:14:coordinate index is the unconditioned law.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:16:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:17:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:18:The generating descriptions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:19:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:21:The restricted laws themselves are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:22:1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:23:-/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:5:# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:7:This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:8:the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:9:is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:10:coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:11:the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:12:point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:13:commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:14:canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:15:field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:16:the same three coordinate ranges.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:17:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:18:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:19:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:20:The decompositions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:21:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:22:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:23:The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:24:445--480, paper lines 970--989.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:25:-/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:67:/-- Split an extended point into its two source point blocks and its two

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:109:          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:139:/-! ## Transport to the source scalar field -/
